# SB-1004 Safety bulletin: airborne dust from blasting

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-HP02

Hazard description
- Background: Blasting operations on line P1-L4 generate airborne particulate that can migrate into adjacent work areas and into the Heat Treat cell housing forging presses. Airborne dust includes abrasive media fines, dressing material, and oxide from forged components. When inhaled, respirable particulates can cause acute irritation and contribute to chronic respiratory conditions. Dust deposition on press surfaces and hydraulic connections increases the risk of contamination of hydraulic fluid and seal wear, and it can impair sensors and guards. Dust accumulations on electrical enclosures and moving parts can also alter heat dissipation and increase the likelihood of unplanned maintenance.
- Pathway and exposure rationale: Blasting plumes produced during open blasting and during abrasive transfer are driven by air movement in the cell and by operator interaction with parts. Without adequate capture and control at the source, particulates follow airflow into adjacent process equipment and into the hot work envelope of forging presses, including Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02). Once inside press housings or fluid reservoirs, particulates can abrade components and contaminate hydraulic circuits, degrading performance and increasing maintenance burden.
- Examples observed: Visual inspections documented dust on exterior press surfaces, grit in access panel seams, and dust tracking into hydraulic fill access areas. Housekeeping records showed repeat cleaning in the blasting cell and immediate perimeter prior to press operation.

Affected equipment
- Scope: All equipment on line P1-L4 within the blasting cell perimeter and immediate work corridors are affected. Specific emphasis is placed on Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) due to its proximity to blasting operations and observed ingress points. Other nearby presses and peripheral handling equipment are within the potential exposure zone and must be considered during control implementation.
- Lubrication note: The lubricant part number for Heat Treat hydraulic forging press #2 (EQ-P1-L4-HP02) is CFW-LUB-195.
- Interfaces: Access panels, hydraulic fill points, vent stacks, and electrical enclosures on affected equipment are potential entry points for dust. Any gap in seals or maintenance access can permit particulate entry during and after blasting operations.

Required controls
- Hierarchy and rationale: Apply a layered control approach with engineering controls prioritized, supported by administrative controls and personal protective equipment. Engineering controls reduce source generation and intercept migration; administrative controls manage procedure and sequencing; PPE protects workers from residual exposure.
- Engineering controls:
  - Contain blasting operations using enclosures and local capture. Enclosure use limits plume spread and protects adjacent equipment and personnel.
  - Ensure blasting media transfer and storage use closed systems or covered containers to prevent secondary releases.
  - Install or verify functioning local exhaust ventilation at blasting locations and ensure exhaust is routed to filtration before discharge to work areas.
  - Improve sealing of press housings and verify intact door and panel seals to prevent dust ingress.
  - Provide positive-pressure clean air purging for critical electronics or hydraulic reservoirs where design allows.
- Administrative controls:
  - Schedule blasting and press operation sequencing to minimize concurrent exposures when practical. Coordinate with maintenance and operations to avoid open equipment during active blasting.
  - Require advance notification to press operators and maintenance personnel before blasting begins in adjacent cells.
  - Implement targeted housekeeping procedures for blasting perimeter and affected equipment at the close of blasting activities and before press start-up.
  - Update SOPs cited below to incorporate blasting-specific precautions for P1-L4 line activities.
- Personnel protection and work practices:
  - Use appropriate respiratory protection in blasting perimeter work areas per existing respiratory protection program. Select PPE based on exposure assessment.
  - Limit entry to affected zones to essential personnel during active blasting and until post-blast cleanup is complete.
  - Train operators and maintenance staff on dust ingress risks, seal inspection, and contamination control practices.
- Records and verification:
  - Maintain blasting logs documenting times, media used, and capture system status for each blasting event near line P1-L4.
  - Keep inspection records for press seals, access panels, and hydraulic fill access for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 and adjacent equipment.
  - Retain housekeeping completion records showing cleaning actions performed after blasting and prior to press operations.
  - Document notifications and coordination activities between blasting crews and press operations.

Records to keep and where to file
- Blasting event log: File in the blasting cell control binder and upload to the document control system referenced by SOP-P1-L4-04.
- Press inspection checklist: Save in the maintenance folder for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 and reference in work order history.
- Housekeeping verification: Retain in the line P1-L4 daily housekeeping records as required by SOP-P1-L4-05.
- Incident and corrective action records: Follow reporting pathways in SB-1034 for any event involving contamination of hydraulic systems or unplanned press downtime attributed to dust ingress.

Effective date
- Effective date: Immediate

Related documents
- See SB-1034 for incident reporting and corrective action procedures.
- Consult SOP-P1-L4-04 for blasting operation controls and logkeeping requirements.
- Consult SOP-P1-L4-05 for housekeeping and cleaning verification procedures.

Action items
- Operations and maintenance leads must review this bulletin and update local checklists to ensure the controls above are in place for line P1-L4.
- Maintenance must confirm the lubricant part number CFW-LUB-195 is used for EQ-P1-L4-HP02 and record verification in the equipment maintenance folder.
- Blasting supervisors must ensure capture and enclosure practices are validated and documented per SOP-P1-L4-04 before resuming operations adjacent to affected equipment.
